subject: extracting information from a fitted lavaan object

messages.author: aa2236293b0acbb4
messages.subject: extracting information from a fitted lavaan object
parts:
Hello,

I fitted a mediation model with the following code: 

model1 <- '
# measurement model
PF =~ 1*rand9 + p8*rand10
V =~ 1*rand23 + v2*rand27
GH =~ gh1*rand1 + gh5*rand36
# regression model
GH ~ b1*V + b2*PF + c1*gender + c2*lf
V ~ b3*PF + c3*gender + c4*lf
# variances of latent variables
GH ~~ e1*GH
V ~~ e2*V
PF ~~ e3*PF
# covariances of observed variables
lf ~~ gender
PF ~~ gender
PF ~~ lf
# new parameters
M := b3 * b1
'

I would like to extract the value of the new parameter M from the fitted model output because I need to work with it further. 
I have been using the following code to extract eg path b1 : 
model1_fit <- sem(model = model, data = dat_rel_complete)
lavInspect(model1_fit, what = "std.all")$beta[3,2]
but lavInspect does not allow me to extract the new parameter M in the same way.

Any help is highly appreciated!

Rebecca

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: extracting information from a fitted lavaan object
parts:
Dear Rebecca,

The call to lavInspect() you used only give you the parameter estimates in the model matrices. The M you defined is a derived parameter that does not exist in the matrix.

The following is one possible way to get what you need, if you only need the standardized estimate and not its SE:

``` r
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-15
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
dat <- HolzingerSwineford1939
mod <-
"
x2 ~ a * x1
x3 ~ b * x2
ab := a * b
"
fit <- sem(mod, data = dat)
est <- parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE)
print(est, nd = 7)
#>   lhs op rhs label       est        se         z   pvalue  ci.lower  ci.upper
#> 1  x2  ~  x1     a 0.2998972 0.0555043  5.403136 1.00e-07 0.1911108 0.4086836
#> 2  x3  ~  x2     b 0.3264360 0.0520689  6.269309 0.00e+00 0.2243828 0.4284891
#> 3  x2 ~~  x2       1.2596143 0.1026761 12.267844 0.00e+00 1.0583729 1.4608558
#> 4  x3 ~~  x3       1.1276214 0.0919168 12.267844 0.00e+00 0.9474677 1.3077751
#> 5  x1 ~~  x1       1.3583698 0.0000000        NA       NA 1.3583698 1.3583698
#> 6  ab := a*b    ab 0.0978972 0.0239191  4.092854 4.26e-05 0.0510167 0.1447777
#>      std.lv   std.all   std.nox
#> 1 0.2998972 0.2973455 0.2551246
#> 2 0.3264360 0.3398490 0.3398490
#> 3 1.2596143 0.9115856 0.9115856
#> 4 1.1276214 0.8845027 0.8845027
#> 5 1.3583698 1.0000000 1.3583698
#> 6 0.0978972 0.1010526 0.0867038
est[est$lhs == "ab", "std.all"]
#> [1] 0.1010526
```

Use parameterEstimates() instead. It computes the user-defined parameters.

I like base R but you certainly can use other methods you like to extract value.

If you need SE of the standardized estimate, then you would need to use standardizedSolution().

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: AW: extracting information from a fitted lavaan object
parts:
Well, your self-defined parameter is not included in the matrix. In any case, I would proceed differently when extracting the parameters. There are several solutions that are more convenient and safer than specifying the position in a matrix:

library(lavaan)

data <- simulateData(
  "
  PF =~ 1 * rand9 + 1 * rand10
  V =~ 1 * rand23 + 1 * rand27
  GH =~ 1 * rand1 + 1 * rand36
  GH ~ 0.4  * V + 0.2 * PF
  V ~ 0.2 * PF
  ",
  sample.nobs = 1000
)

model1 <- '
# measurement model
PF =~ 1*rand9 + p8*rand10
V =~ 1*rand23 + v2*rand27
GH =~ gh1*rand1 + gh5*rand36
# regression model
GH ~ b1*V + b2*PF

# new parameters
M := b3 * b1
'

fit <- sem(model1, data)

# Solution 1
coef(fit, type = "user")["M"]

# Solution 2
pe <- parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE)
pe[pe$label == "M", "est"]            # Unstandardized coefs
pe[pe$label == "M", "std.all"]        # Standardized coefs
